title: Asking with onko with singular owners
summary: Ask with onko and minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.
objectives: Ask with onko and minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Ask with onko and minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.
Add the yes/no question ending -ko to on: on + -ko = onko. Put onko first, then the owner, then one thing in its basic singular form.
keyPoints: Ask with onko and minulla, sinulla, and hänellä.

steps: Start with on (“have” here) and add the yes/no question ending -ko: on + -ko = onko.
minulla means “I as the owner”. Put the owner after onko.
kirja (“book”) stays in its basic singular form at the end.
The question word remains onko with sinulla; do not use oletko from an “Are you …?” sentence.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person. Put the owner after onko.
koira (“dog”) stays in its basic singular form at the end.
Onko stays the same whether hänellä is translated with “he” or “she”.
hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”. Put the owner after onko.
auto (“car”) stays in its basic singular form at the end.
Changing the noun changes what is asked about, not onko.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person. Put the owner after onko.
kissa (“cat”) stays in its basic singular form at the end.

commonMistakes: Add -ko to fixed on to form onko with minulla, sinulla and hänellä.
Put Onko before the owner: Onko sinulla pallo? The statement Sinulla on pallo is not the requested question.
Keep the noun form shown in the task. This pack models basic singular nouns; partitive questions are also natural in other contexts.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.formation: On + the yes/no question ending -ko = onko. It stays the same with every possessor.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
kynä stays in its basic singular form: one pen.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed onko in possession questions: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
